criteria.reason: Passing test asserts chain true, HANDOFF line, banner null, notify false, chainSkill null and chainSteps sweep/verify/implement args.
Passing test asserts the four steps in order with implement false; the no-chain tests assert chain false.
Passing test asserts chain false for both a hit and status invalid with implement true.
Passing test asserts fold-back for notSweepItems/overlap with deduplicated ids.
Passing test asserts verify after a clean sweep.
Passing test asserts commit after satisfied with a clean sweep brake.
Passing test asserts commit after fold-back with sweepIdsLeft [] and no verification outcome.
Direct run and passing Jest show stop with STUCK banner, body and notifyStatus for stalled, stuck, unbuilt and insufficient-coverage.
Passing test asserts stop (not commit) with auth/x.js named in bannerBody.
Passing test asserts implement after commit with coreTrdExists true and no core brake hit.

After a fold-back, a core-TRD hit and an invalid core list each stop with a COMMAND STUCK banner. The after-commit branch ignores the core check's result, but by design that check runs only after a fold-back, and the fold-back stop comes before any commit. Without a fold-back, plan() itself refuses to chain when the core TRD is hit. So no reachable path reaches implement with a core hit.
sweepChainNext returns fold-back only after the sweep step. The direct run, given an already-folded state with more foldable ids, returns verify and then commit, never a second fold-back.
Fixture runs show hits [src/auth/login.js] for 'Paths: auth' and status invalid for a malformed 5b list.
plan.md switches to the feature branch before /sweep and lets sweepChainNext alone pick each next step. It emits nothing after the implement step's Skill() call; a stop prints the banner.
sweep.md strips the flags first and defers any item whose fix would touch a never-unattended path (sweep.md line 65). It ends with the RETURN line and no banner.
Under --chained, not-a-sweep-item and overlapping ids are written to sweep-result.json as notSweepItems and overlap instead of ending STUCK, and Step 4 records no _sweep discovery for them.
Under --chained on a sweep file, verify-build.md asks nothing (stated default), still writes the report and carries the evidence to the core, and ends with the RETURN line and no banner.
The fold-back lists all seven steps in the specified order, never re-runs /sweep, and skips render-sweep when no sweep id remains.

plan.md's commit step records git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all and git hash-object per path before /sweep and compares both after; the list adds the sweep file and .trd-state/<slug>-sweep/; the never-unattended check runs over the whole list before git add; staging is git add -- <list> then git commit -- <list>; git diff --cached --quiet -- <list> skips the commit and continues, never an empty commit. The artifact matches the source text, and the .claude mirror is identical.
The chaining-exception paragraph in the template names /sweep --chained and /verify-build --chained emitting no banner inside /plan --implement. The vendored copy is identical.
